author: Xu Han
note: Learning/portfolio demonstrator. NOT a calibrated observatory simulator, NOT an exposure-time calculator, NOT a reproduction of HARMONI/MUSE/NIRSpec, and NOT a validated performance prediction.
snr_interpretation: median_line_snr includes bad-pixel-zeroed spaxels, so a masked pixel in the line window pulls a single-row (nearest / trace-offset) method's aperture median to 0.0. That is a reduction limitation of single-row extraction, not a physical non-detection: read finite_snr_fraction (usable spaxel fraction) and median_line_snr_finite_only (median over usable spaxels) alongside it. The weighted Horne extraction spans several rows, so a single bad row rarely zeroes a spaxel and its finite fraction stays high.
limitations: Controlled inverse mapping, not a real reduction pipeline.
Weighted/optimal extraction can over-count flux from closely packed traces (fc > 1).
Per-method SNR pairs each flux estimator with its own propagated variance (nearest look-up vs Horne Var=1/sum(P^2/V)); covariance between voxels is not propagated.
median_line_snr=0.0 for single-row methods means bad pixels in the line window, not a non-detection (see finite_snr_fraction / median_line_snr_finite_only).
Trace offset biases flux and velocity; covariance proxy is illustrative only.
